question.problem:
The weights of the wooden and steel chairs produced by a furniture company have standard deviations of $2\,\text{lb}$ and $1\,\text{lb},$ respectively. The company wants to determine whether the population mean ${\mu }_{x}$ of weights for the wooden chairs is greater than the population mean ${\mu }_{y}$ of weights for the steel chairs. They construct a $95%$ confidence interval for the difference between the population means.

Given that the company sampled $100$ wooden chairs and $150$ steel chairs and found that their mean weights are $10\,\text{lb}$ and $9\,\text{lb},$ respectively, which of the following statements are true?

I. The end-points of the $95%$ confidence interval for the difference between the population means are approximately $1\pm 0.423.$

II. All values contained within the $95%$ confidence interval are positive.

III. The confidence interval data suggests that ${\mu }_{x}>{\mu }_{y}.$

*Hint: Given a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ the table below shows the $z$-scores ${z}_{p}$ such that $P(Z>{z}_{p})=p$ for some particular values of $p.$*

| $p$ | $0.100$ | $0.050$ | $0.025$ | $0.010$ | $0.005$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${z}_{p}$ | $1.282$ | $1.645$ | $1.960$ | $2.326$ | $2.576$ |
